content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a plant enrichment from used teabags, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Collect used organic tea bags (3 days)
Step 2. Shred the tea bag paper casing (10 minutes)
Step 3. Remove metal staples from tea bags (5 minutes)
Step 4. Sterilize the mixing bowl (5 minutes)
Step 5. Store the final enrichment in an airtight jar (2 minutes)
Step 6. Spread damp leaves on a drying tray (10 minutes)
Step 7. Squeeze out excess liquid from bags (3 minutes)
Step 8. Measure the weight of the dried leaves (2 minutes)
Step 9. Harvest leaves from steeped bags (15 minutes)
Step 10. Clean the workstation (15 minutes)
Step 11. Sift the dried leaves to remove large stems (10 minutes)
Step 12. Dehydrate the tea leaves in the sun (6 hours)
Step 13. Mix shredded paper with dried leaves (5 minutes)
Step 14. Add a spoonful of molasses to the mixture (1 minute)
Step 15. Compost the leftover tea strings (1 minute)
Step 16. Grind the leaves into a fine powder (8 minutes)
Step 17. Rinse the mixing spoon (30 seconds)
Step 18. Open the tea bags carefully (20 minutes)
Step 19. Label the batch with the date (1 minute)
Step 20. Test the pH level of the mixture (5 minutes)
Step 21. Soak the leaves in distilled water (12 hours)
Step 22. Sanitize the cutting shears (4 minutes)
Step 23. Drain the tea leaves through a fine mesh (5 minutes)
Step 24. Measure a teaspoon of cinnamon as a fungicide (30 seconds)
Step 25. Calibrate the kitchen scale (2 minutes)
Step 26. Seal the dry components in a bag (1 minute)
Step 27. Combine all ingredients into the final blend (10 minutes)
Step 28. Purchase a moisture meter (1 hour)
Step 29. Pour the tea liquid into a spray bottle (2 minutes)
Step 30. Incorporate the shredded paper into the wet mix (5 minutes)
Step 31. Apply the enrichment to the soil (15 minutes)
Step 32. Gather all necessary tools (10 minutes)
Step 33. Sprinkle the mixture over the plant roots (10 minutes)
Step 34. Aerate the liquid infusion (24 hours)
Step 35. Filter the liquid through a coffee filter (15 minutes)
Step 36. Decant the concentrated liquid (5 minutes)
Step 37. Document the recipe in a garden log (10 minutes)
Step 38. Sharpen the gardening trowel (15 minutes)
Step 39. Set up a dedicated workspace (20 minutes)
Step 40. Inspect bags for mold (5 minutes)
